storyBeats.text: The garage was yours. This isn't. There's a sign-up sheet by the door, a guy running sound who'd rather be anywhere else, and eleven other acts. You get three songs on Tuesday. Take them. Then take Friday.

By now the calendar runs itself - Tuesdays, the house parties, the coffeehouse guy who finally started calling you. The talent show is the one night that isn't routine, and you win it anyway. A woman who books the club on Third finds you at the load-out and asks what else you've got. Dave's already got the van running.

sections.title: The Calendar
sections.description: The nights you have booked. Pick a gig to play it, tap its row to work the crowd, and read your running totals on the lines above.

sections.title: Bookings
sections.description: A gig's draw is how many people turn up for it. Buy the draw and that gig pays more cash and more fans every time you finish the set.

sections.title: Promotion
sections.description: Handbills, mailing lists and anyone who will write about you. They build Buzz on their own, and every point of Buzz adds a little to the cash a gig pays.

sections.title: The Office
sections.description: Where the band's business gets done. A standing booking makes a gig repeat itself, and the rest buys you more out of every night you play.

sections.title: The Release
sections.description: Record an EP once you have 300 fans. It banks Records and EPs and starts the run over with the calendar empty.

sections.title: Battle of the Bands
sections.description: Three timed rounds, one at a time. The run starts over for each one, and clearing a round doubles what every gig pays for the rest of the chapter.

sections.title: The Talent Show
sections.description: The night that ends the chapter. Record 120 EPs to get on the bill, and you walk away with another Roadie.

bars.description: A five-second set that fills on its own clock and pays your open mic draw when it lands.
Fifteen seconds in somebody's living room, paying your house party draw every time it fills.
Forty seconds for the coffee crowd, paying your coffeehouse draw when the set finishes.
Two minutes in a backyard, paying your backyard show draw each time the set lands.
Five minutes opening for somebody else, paying your bar opening slot draw when the set is done.
Twelve minutes at the top of the ladder, paying your qualifier draw every time it fills.

generators.description: How many people turn up for you on a Tuesday, and every level pays a bigger lump of Cash and Fans when the set ends.

How many tables fill up for the coffeehouse set, and every level pays a bigger lump of Cash and Fans when the set finishes.
How much of the neighborhood walks over for the backyard show, and every level pays a bigger lump of Cash and Fans at the end of the night.
How much of the bar's crowd sticks around for your opening slot, and every level pays a bigger lump of Cash and Fans when you come off.

generators.displayName: Battle of the Bands Qualifier Draw
generators.description: How many of your own people show up to the qualifier, and every level pays a bigger lump of Cash and Fans when the night ends.
Another run of flyers stapled to the poles around town, each one building Buzz while you play.
Another page of names who hear about the next show first, and every page builds Buzz faster than a flyer.
Someone who shoots your shows for free, and the pictures going around build Buzz faster than a mailing list.
Another write-up in the local zine, the loudest Buzz in town per printing.

upgrades.description: Puts you on the Tuesday bill for good, so the open mic re-books itself and keeps paying while you are away.
Gets your name on every party going around, so the house party re-books itself and keeps paying while you are away.
The coffeehouse starts calling you itself, so the set re-books itself and keeps paying while you are away.
The neighbors keep asking for another one, so the backyard show re-books itself and keeps paying while you are away.
The bar keeps you on its calendar, so the opening slot re-books itself and keeps paying while you are away.
Your name stays in the qualifier draw, so the night re-books itself and keeps paying while you are away.
Hand the calendar over: every gig buys as many levels as you can afford on its own, for the rest of the chapter.
Everyone in town owes you one, so every gig level costs half for the rest of the chapter.
Talk to the room between songs, and every tap on a gig pushes its bar twice as far.
Get the crowd singing back at you, and every tap pushes a gig's bar further still.
Kids who hand out your flyers for you, so everything in Promotion builds Buzz twice as fast.
Shirts and tapes by the door, so every gig pays more Cash when it ends.
Dave's van gets the gear and a carload of friends to the show, so every gig brings more Fans.
